stories.head: Only 14% of shoppers see consistent product data — GEO and agentic commerce explained
stories.plain: Athos Commerce CMO Gary Lombardo flags that 86% of shoppers encounter inconsistent product data across channels — a foundational problem as AI agents increasingly make purchase decisions on behalf of consumers. He explains how GEO differs from SEO and where brand authority fits in an agentic commerce world, making this directly relevant to anyone buying or building marketing AI.

stories.head: Marketing's seat at the resilience table is theater if it lacks decision power, argues Fusion Risk Management
stories.plain: Richard Barnett argues that marketing leaders who only react to crises — rather than shape resilience strategy — are performing a role, not filling one. As AI automates more customer-facing decisions, this tension over who owns the decision layer grows sharper. Relevant to governance debates about where marketing authority starts and ends in automated systems.

stories.head: ChatGPT Ads roll out in Europe with Adform as a launch partner
stories.plain: OpenAI is now selling ads inside ChatGPT across Europe, with Adform as one of the first programmatic partners. This is a structural shift: AI answer engines are becoming paid media channels, which changes how marketing budgets are allocated and forces brands to think about visibility inside AI-generated responses, not just traditional search results.

stories.head: Magnite and ITN launch agentic AI for local linear TV ad buying
stories.plain: Magnite's Orchestration layer now uses agentic AI to compress a multi-week local TV buying process into hours. This is a real workflow change, not a badge deal — autonomous agents are making and placing media buys in a channel historically locked to manual negotiation, signalling how agentic decisioning will reshape traditional media procurement.

stories.head: Azoma sets out which GEO tools help brands losing traffic to AI answers
stories.plain: Adobe data cited here shows AI-referred retail traffic is now the fastest-growing digital channel, surpassing social and email. Azoma's guidance on what to look for in GEO tooling gives marketers a practical framework for staying visible in ChatGPT, Gemini, Rufus, and Walmart Sparky — the new front doors to commerce.

stories.head: Survey: 95% of IT leaders claim AI readiness but data quality gaps tell a different story
stories.plain: An Akeneo global survey finds almost every organization claims to be AI-ready, yet most have serious data quality and governance gaps underneath that confidence. This matters for MarTech buyers because weak product and customer data is the most common reason AI personalization and agentic tools underperform after deployment.

stories.head: Only 14% of shoppers see consistent brand data — and GEO is changing where brand lives
stories.plain: Athos Commerce CMO Gary Lombardo explains that inconsistent product data reaches 86% of shoppers and why that problem is now acute: AI shopping agents pull structured data feeds directly, so brands with messy or contradictory product information will be misrepresented or skipped entirely in AI-generated recommendations — a GEO and data-quality crisis in one.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: ChatGPT Ads & Generative Search Rewrite Discovery
body: OpenAI's ad infrastructure is now live in Europe, with Adform as a named platform partner — meaning paid media can appear inside ChatGPT conversations for the first time at scale. This is not an experiment; it is a new channel that bypasses traditional search-engine result pages entirely.

Simultaneously, brands are discovering that organic visibility in AI-generated answers requires a different playbook than SEO. Azoma's GEO analysis and the Frontier Airlines case study both show that ranking logic in generative engines rewards structured, factual content over keyword density — forcing a rethink of content investment priorities.

Agile Brand · Frontier Airlines AI search

themes.head: Agentic AI Moves from Hype to Workflow
body: Multiple vendors this month shipped tools where AI acts autonomously across multi-step workflows rather than just answering prompts: Magnite & ITN's agentic solution handles local TV ad buys end-to-end, Nimble converts a single prompt into a full sequence of emails, calls, and human-touch tasks, and FinTurk automates advisor portfolio decisions.

The practical implication is that human roles shift from execution to exception-handling. Richard Barnett's 'seat without decisions is theater' framing captures the governance risk: if the agent makes the call, the human in the room needs genuine override authority or the role is ceremonial.

themes.head: AI Ambition Outrunning Data Foundations
body: Akeneo's survey and a separate IT-leader report both land the same verdict: companies are deploying AI models on top of fragmented, incomplete product and commerce data, which limits what those models can reliably do. The Linnworks CMO makes a related point — automation hides manual workarounds rather than eliminating them.

Box's partnership with OpenAI to connect enterprise content to AI pipelines is a direct response to this gap. The bottleneck is not model capability; it is clean, governed, connected data — and organisations that fix the foundation first will compound their AI returns while others iterate on noise.

themes.head: The Brand Consistency Crisis at 14%
body: Only 14% of shoppers encounter a consistent brand experience across touchpoints — a statistic that reframes the urgency of data unification. Fragmented martech stacks are not just an IT cost problem; they are a direct revenue leak because inconsistency erodes trust at every interaction.

With AI now generating personalised content at scale, the inconsistency risk multiplies: models trained on siloed data will produce siloed outputs. Solving brand coherence therefore requires governance decisions — shared taxonomies, single sources of truth — before AI amplifies the gap rather than closing it.
ev: Agile Brand · Linnworks back-office manual work

themes.head: Trust & Privacy Infrastructure as Competitive Moat
body: Newfold Digital's DigiCert deal, covering six million customers, and KERV.ai's TPN Gold Star certification for streaming privacy both signal that trust infrastructure is becoming a procurement requirement, not a compliance checkbox. Buyers — B2B and B2C — are starting to disqualify vendors who cannot demonstrate verified data hygiene.

As AI systems handle more sensitive personalisation and financial decisions (see FinTurk's advisor automation), the stakes of a trust failure rise sharply. Organisations that invest in certified, auditable privacy and security frameworks now are building a moat that latecomers will find expensive to replicate.

month.takeaway: Every major move this month — new ad channels, agentic workflows, enterprise AI partnerships — is being throttled by the same bottleneck: organisations cannot extract value from AI faster than they can fix the data, consistency, and trust foundations underneath it.
